verses.sloka: पुनरेवं ब्रुवाणं तं भरतं लक्ष्मणाग्रज: ।प्रत्युवाच तत: श्रीमान् ज्ञातिमध्ये ऽभिसत्कृत: ॥ २.१०७.१॥
verses.transliteration: punarevaṁ bruvāṇaṁ taṁ bharataṁ lakṣmaṇāgraja: ।pratyuvāca tata: śrīmān jñātimadhye 'bhisatkṛta: ॥ 2.107.1॥

translations.english: Wellhonoured in the midst of relatives, the celebrated Rama, elder brother of Lakshmana, then said to Bharata who was going to speak again.

verses.sloka: उपपन्नमिदं वाक्यं यत्त्वमेवमभाषथा: ।जात: पुत्रो दशरथात् कैकेय्यां राजसत्तमात् ॥ २.१०७.२॥
verses.transliteration: upapannamidaṁ vākyaṁ yattvamevamabhāṣathā: ।jāta: putro daśarathāt kaikeyyāṁ rājasattamāt ॥ 2.107.2॥

translations.english: Appropriate are the words spoken by you born to the celebrated king Dasaratha through Kaikeyi.
translations.hindi: इन्द्र जिस प्रकार अपने गुरु बृहरपति फे चरण छते हैं, उसी प्रकार रास भी अग्निसम तेजस्वो पुरोहित वसिष्ठ के चरण स्पशे कर, उनके साथ आसन पर बैठ गए

verses.sloka: पुरा भ्रात: पिता न: स मातरं ते समुद्वहन् ।मातामहे समाश्रौषीद्राज्यशुल्कमनुत्तमम् ॥ २.१०७.३॥
verses.transliteration: purā bhrāta: pitā na: sa mātaraṁ te samudvahan ।mātāmahe samāśrauṣīdrājyaśulkamanuttamam ॥ 2.107.3॥

translations.english: Earlier when our father was to wed your mother, O dear brother, he had promised to your maternal grandfather that he would confer (on her) a kingdom with good revenue.

verses.sloka: दैवासुरे च सङ्ग्रामे जनन्यै तव पार्थिव: ।सम्प्रहृष्टो ददौ राजा वरमाराधित: प्रभु: ॥ २.१०७.४॥
verses.transliteration: daivāsure ca saṅgrāme jananyai tava pārthiva: ।samprahṛṣṭo dadau rājā varamārādhita: prabhu: ॥ 2.107.4॥

translations.english: Thereafter in the battle between gods and demons, the able king (Dasaratha) pleased (with your mother) granted her a boon (as a token of gratitude).

verses.sloka: तत: सा सम्प्रतिश्राव्य तव माता यशस्विनी ।अयाचत नरश्रेष्ठं द्वौ वरौ वरवर्णिनी ॥ २.१०७.५॥
verses.transliteration: tata: sā sampratiśrāvya tava mātā yaśasvinī ।ayācata naraśreṣṭhaṁ dvau varau varavarṇinī ॥ 2.107.5॥

translations.english: Thereafter, O tiger among men, your illustrious mother of fair complexion, under oath demanded of that best of men, king Dasaratha, the two boons, namely kingdom for you and banishment for me. Bound by such agreement (oath), the king granted her the boons.

verses.sloka: तव राज्यं नरव्याघ्र मम प्रव्राजनं तथा ।तौ च राजा तदा तस्यै नियुक्त: प्रददौ वरौ ॥ २.१०७.६॥
verses.transliteration: tava rājyaṁ naravyāghra mama pravrājanaṁ tathā ।tau ca rājā tadā tasyai niyukta: pradadau varau ॥ 2.107.6॥

translations.english: Thereafter, O tiger among men, your illustrious mother of fair complexion, under oath demanded of that best of men, king Dasaratha, the two boons, namely kingdom for you and banishment for me. Bound by such agreement (oath), the king granted her the boons.

verses.sloka: तेन पित्रा ऽहमप्यत्र नियुक्त: पुरुषर्षभ ।चतुर्दश वने वासं वर्षाणि वरदानिकम् ॥ २.१०७.७॥
verses.transliteration: tena pitrā 'hamapyatra niyukta: puruṣarṣabha ।caturdaśa vane vāsaṁ varṣāṇi varadānikam ॥ 2.107.7॥

translations.english: O best of men, that is why I have been ordered by father to live in the forest for fourteen years as per the (condition of the) boon.

verses.sloka: सो ऽहं वनमिदं प्राप्तो निर्जनं लक्ष्मणान्वित: ।सीतया चाप्रतिद्वन्द्व: सत्यवादे स्थित: पितु: ॥ २.१०७.८॥
verses.transliteration: so 'haṁ vanamidaṁ prāpto nirjanaṁ lakṣmaṇānvita: ।sītayā cāpratidvandva: satyavāde sthita: pitu: ॥ 2.107.8॥

translations.english: I have come to this lonely forest accompanied by Lakshmana and Sita, bent upon upholding the truth of our unrivalled father's words.

verses.sloka: भवानपि तथेत्येव पितरं सत्यवादिनम् ।कर्त्तुमर्हति राजेन्द्र क्षिप्रमेवाभिषेचनात् ॥ २.१०७.९॥
verses.transliteration: bhavānapi tathetyeva pitaraṁ satyavādinam ।karttumarhati rājendra kṣipramevābhiṣecanāt ॥ 2.107.9॥

translations.english: O Indra among kings, let your coronation be performed without delay since you are worthy and at the same time the truthfulness of our father's words be honoured.

verses.sloka: ऋणान्मोचय राजानं मत्कृते भरत प्रभुम् ।पितरं चापि धर्मज्ञं मातरं चाभिनन्दय ॥ २.१०७.१०॥
verses.transliteration: ṛṇānmocaya rājānaṁ matkṛte bharata prabhum ।pitaraṁ cāpi dharmajñaṁ mātaraṁ cābhinandaya ॥ 2.107.10॥

translations.english: O Bharata, release for my sake the competent king from his debt (of vow) and honour the righteous father and the mother as well.

verses.sloka: श्रूयते हि पुरा तात श्रुतिर्गीता यशस्विना ।गयेन यजमानेन गयेष्वेव पितऽन् प्रति ॥ २.१०७.११॥
verses.transliteration: śrūyate hi purā tāta śrutirgītā yaśasvinā ।gayena yajamānena gayeṣveva pita'n prati ॥ 2.107.11॥

translations.english: Dear (brother), it is heard that long ago an illustrious king while performing a sacrifice intended for ancestors at a sacred place known as Gaya, the sacrificer Gaya chanted a Vedic hymn as follows:

verses.sloka: पुन्नाम्नो नरकाद्यस्मात् पितरं त्रायते सुत: ।तस्मात् पुत्र इति प्रोक्त: पितऽन् यत्पाति वा सुत: ॥ २.१०७.१२॥
verses.transliteration: punnāmno narakādyasmāt pitaraṁ trāyate suta: ।tasmāt putra iti prokta: pita'n yatpāti vā suta: ॥ 2.107.12॥

translations.english: Putra is so called as he delivers his father from a hell known as Put and protects the ancestors in all possible ways.

verses.sloka: एष्टव्या बहव: पुत्रा गुणवन्तो बहुश्रुता: ।तेषां वै समवेतानामपि कश्चिद्गयां व्रजेत् ॥ २.१०७.१३॥
verses.transliteration: eṣṭavyā bahava: putrā guṇavanto bahuśrutā: ।teṣāṁ vai samavetānāmapi kaścidgayāṁ vrajet ॥ 2.107.13॥

translations.english: One should desire many virtuous and learned sons so that at least one of them may go to Gaya (to perform the father's obsequies).

verses.sloka: एवं राजर्षय: सर्वे प्रतीता राजनन्दन ।तस्मात् त्राहि नरश्रेष्ठ पितरं नरकात् प्रभो ॥ २.१०७.१४॥
verses.transliteration: evaṁ rājarṣaya: sarve pratītā rājanandana ।tasmāt trāhi naraśreṣṭha pitaraṁ narakāt prabho ॥ 2.107.14॥

translations.english: O enhancer of the king's delight, O best of men rajarsis have decided this way. You may, therefore, O lord, protect your father against hell.

verses.sloka: अयोध्यां गच्छ भरत प्रकृतीरनुरञ्जय ।शत्रुघ्नसहितो वीर सह सर्वैर्द्विजातिभि: ॥ २.१०७.१५॥
verses.transliteration: ayodhyāṁ gaccha bharata prakṛtīranurañjaya ।śatrughnasahito vīra saha sarvairdvijātibhi: ॥ 2.107.15॥

translations.english: O valiant Bharata, go to Ayodhya accompanied by Satrughna and the twiceborn (brahmins) and keep the subjects delighted like pleased (with your rule).

verses.sloka: प्रवेक्ष्ये दण्डकारण्यमहमप्यविलम्बयन् ।आभ्यां तु सहितो राजन् वैदेह्या लक्ष्मणेन च ॥ २.१०७.१६॥
verses.transliteration: pravekṣye daṇḍakāraṇyamahamapyavilambayan ।ābhyāṁ tu sahito rājan vaidehyā lakṣmaṇena ca ॥ 2.107.16॥

translations.english: O king (Bharata) I shall also enter the Dandaka forest without delay in the company of only these two -- the princess from Videha (Sita) and Lakshmana.

verses.sloka: त्वं राजा भरत भव स्वयं नराणां वन्यानामहमपि राजराण्मृगाणाम् ।गच्छत्वं पुरवरमद्य सम्प्रहृष्ट: संहृष्टस्त्वहमपि दण्डकान् प्रवेक्ष्ये ॥ २.१०७.१७॥
verses.transliteration: tvaṁ rājā bharata bhava svayaṁ narāṇāṁ vanyānāmahamapi rājarāṇmṛgāṇām ।gacchatvaṁ puravaramadya samprahṛṣṭa: saṁhṛṣṭastvahamapi daṇḍakān pravekṣye ॥ 2.107.17॥

translations.english: O Bharata, be the king of men. I shall also become the supreme king of the wild beasts in the forest. Go now happily to Ayodhya, the best of cities, and I shall enter Dandaka forest with delight.

verses.sloka: छायां ते दिनकरभा: प्रबाधमानं वर्षत्रं भरत करोतु मूर्ध्नि शीताम् ।एतेषामहमपि काननद्रुमाणां छायां तामति शयिनीं सुखी श्रयिष्ये ॥ २.१०७.१८॥
verses.transliteration: chāyāṁ te dinakarabhā: prabādhamānaṁ varṣatraṁ bharata karotu mūrdhni śītām ।eteṣāmahamapi kānanadrumāṇāṁ chāyāṁ tāmati śayinīṁ sukhī śrayiṣye ॥ 2.107.18॥

translations.english: Let an umbrella protect you against (scorching) sunshine and provide its cool shade over your head, O Bharata As for me, I shall happily seek the shade of these dense woodland trees.

verses.sloka: शत्रुघ्न: कुशलमतिस्तु ते सहाय: सौमित्रिर्मम विदित: प्रधानमित्रम् ।चत्वारस्तनयवरा वयं नरेन्द्रं सत्यस्थं भरत चराम मा विषादम् ॥ २.१०७.१९ ॥
verses.transliteration: śatrughna: kuśalamatistu te sahāya: saumitrirmama vidita: pradhānamitram ।catvārastanayavarā vayaṁ narendraṁ satyasthaṁ bharata carāma mā viṣādam ॥ 2.107.19 ॥

translations.english: O Bharata, intelligent Satrughna will be your support and son of Sumitra (Lakshmana) as is wellknown will remain my best friend. All four of us, worthy sons of Dasaratha, shall follow the path of truth of our father. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे सप्तोत्तरशततमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the one hundredseventh sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
